items.name: South Indian filter coffee
items.prabhava: Chicory-blended decoction with hot frothed milk — milk and sugar blunt coffee's vata edge; still a stimulant that borrows from tomorrow.
items.preparation: Slow-drip decoction through the brass filter, mixed with hot milk and modest sugar; one strong morning tumbler is the tradition.

items.name: Sweet lime juice
items.prabhava: The hospital-visit juice of India — gentle, hydrating, low-acid citrus that sits well on weak and feverish digestion.
combinations: fresh-pressed with a pinch of rock salt
items.preparation: Fresh-pressed and drunk promptly, unsweetened or lightly salted; the gentlest citrus for convalescence.

items.name: Pomegranate juice
items.prabhava: Dadima svarasa is the classical heart-and-blood juice — tridoshic, digestive without heating; the most praised fruit juice of the tradition.
combinations: a pinch of rock salt for weak agni
contraindications: medication interactions (grapefruit-like enzyme effects at high daily volumes)
items.preparation: Press fresh sweet arils and drink promptly; bottled versions lose the prana and gain the sugar.

items.name: Orange juice
combinations: room temperature, never iced with meals
viruddha: with milk or dairy breakfast items (curdles — the cereal-and-OJ trap)
items.preparation: Fresh-pressed from sweet oranges; drink alone — its sourness quarrels with milk and grains at the same table.

items.name: Ash gourd juice
items.prabhava: The modern-classical morning cooler — kushmanda's medhya (mind-clearing) coolness in a glass; strong pitta constitutions thrive on it, cold constitutions don't.
combinations: fresh on an empty stomach (pitta protocols)
with a pinch of rock salt or lime
contraindications: raw juice needs a clean fresh gourd
items.preparation: Juice fresh peeled ash gourd and drink within minutes; skip it on cold, damp days — this is a hot-season, hot-constitution drink.

items.name: Bottle gourd juice
items.prabhava: Lauki's lightness as a morning drink — cooling and diuretic; carries one absolute rule: taste first, discard if bitter.
combinations: with mint and a pinch of rock salt
with a little ginger for cold constitutions
contraindications: BITTER JUICE MUST BE DISCARDED — cucurbitacin toxicity from bitter gourds is dangerous
items.preparation: Taste the raw gourd first; juice only sweet lauki, drink fresh. The bitterness rule is a safety rule, not a taste preference.

items.name: Carrot juice
combinations: blended with beet and amla (winter juice tradition)
contraindications: carotenemia (harmless skin tint, very large daily amounts)
items.preparation: Fresh-pressed winter carrots, drunk promptly; a little ginger keeps it moving.

items.name: Beetroot juice
items.prabhava: Concentrated blood-builder of the winter juice tradition; modern evidence adds nitrate-linked circulation support — intense enough to dilute.
combinations: diluted with carrot or cucumber juice
items.preparation: Always dilute — half beet, half carrot or water; sip rather than gulp.

items.name: Herbal kadha
items.prabhava: The household decoction — tulsi, ginger, pepper, cinnamon boiled down by half; kvatha is the classical dosage form for driving warmth into cold, damp congestion.
viruddha: honey into boiling-hot kadha (add lukewarm only)
contraindications: high pitta, acidity (strong daily kadha — the 2020 over-use lesson)
not a daily-forever drink; a weather-and-season tool
items.preparation: Simmer the spices in water reduced by half, strain, honey when lukewarm; use during cold-wet weather, not year-round.

items.name: Fennel water
items.prabhava: Fennel steeped in water — the cooling spice-water; settles gas and acidity without heating, safe across constitutions and seasons.
combinations: soaked overnight and drunk on waking (pitta)
items.preparation: Soak 1 tsp fennel overnight in a cup of water, or steep in hot water 10 minutes; the gentlest of the spice waters.

items.name: Cumin water
items.prabhava: Boiled cumin water — the postpartum and everyday digestive drink; warms the gut, moves gas, gently supports lactation by tradition.
combinations: boiled and sipped warm through the day
with a pinch of rock salt for bloating
items.preparation: Boil 1 tsp cumin in 2 cups water for 5 minutes, strain into a flask; the workhorse of the spice waters.

items.name: Ajwain water
items.prabhava: The strongest spice water — ajwain's thymol heat for cramping, gas and cold sluggish digestion; the postpartum staple of North Indian homes.
combinations: with a pinch of black salt for gas
contraindications: pregnancy (medicinal strength; postpartum is the tradition, not pregnancy)
items.preparation: Boil 1/2 tsp ajwain in 2 cups water for 5 minutes; stronger medicine than jeera water — use when digestion actually struggles.

items.name: Fenugreek water
items.prabhava: Overnight-soaked fenugreek water — the blood-sugar-tradition morning drink; bitter warmth with a mucilaginous softness rare among heating drinks.
combinations: soaked overnight, drunk on waking, seeds chewed after
alternating with jeera water through the week
contraindications: pregnancy (uterine-stimulant tradition — avoid medicinal daily use)
items.preparation: Soak 1 tsp seeds overnight; drink the water and chew the softened seeds. Traditional support, no medical claims.

items.name: Coriander seed water
items.prabhava: The classical cold infusion (hima) for pitta — coriander's rare cooling digestion; the burning-urination and acidity home remedy of the tradition.
combinations: with a little mishri for pitta heat
items.preparation: Soak 1 tsp crushed coriander seeds overnight in a cup of room-temperature water, strain and drink — the hima method preserves its coolness.

items.name: Ragi malt (beverage)
items.prabhava: Finger-millet porridge-drink — calcium-dense cooling breakfast of Karnataka and Andhra; sprouted-ragi versions are the traditional infant strengthener.
contraindications: cold constitutions in winter (a summer-leaning drink)
items.preparation: Cook ragi flour in water to a pourable porridge; finish salty with buttermilk or sweet with milk-jaggery.

items.name: Black carrot kanji
items.prabhava: Winter-sun fermented black carrots with mustard and salt — North India's living probiotic drink; kanjika appears in classical sour-ferment lists.
combinations: small glasses before or with lunch
items.preparation: Ferment black carrot batons in salted mustard water in winter sun for 3–5 days until pleasingly sour; refrigerate once ready.
provenance: North Indian tradition; kanjika in classical lists

items.name: Pakhala (fermented water-rice)
items.prabhava: Odisha's summer institution — rice fermented in water overnight, eaten with the tangy torani liquid; cools field workers through the fiercest heat.
combinations: with roasted vegetables, curd and fried accompaniments (traditional platter)
torani (the liquid) sipped as a drink
items.preparation: Soak cooked rice in water overnight with a little old torani as starter; eat at midday with salt, curd and sides.

items.name: Ambali (fermented ragi porridge)
items.prabhava: Overnight-fermented ragi porridge thinned with buttermilk — the millet-revival movement's favorite gut drink, with deep Deccan roots.
combinations: with buttermilk, salt and curry leaves
items.preparation: Cook ragi porridge, cool, ferment overnight in a clay pot, then thin with buttermilk and salt.

items.name: Gundruk (fermented greens)
items.prabhava: Nepal's national ferment — sun-dried soured leafy greens whose sharp tang carries mountain kitchens through winter without fresh vegetables.
combinations: gundruk soup with potato and tomato
items.preparation: Rehydrate briefly and cook into tangy soup; a little goes far — it is condiment-intensity, not salad.

items.name: Sinki (fermented radish)
items.prabhava: Pit-fermented radish taproot of the eastern Himalaya — pungent-sour winter condiment that cuts through cold-weather heaviness.
items.preparation: Rehydrate and simmer into sour soup; the radish sharpness survives fermentation — season accordingly.

items.name: Fermented bamboo shoot (soibum)
items.prabhava: Manipur's signature ferment — bamboo shoots soured in their own culture; the electric tang beneath eromba and kangsoi.
contraindications: thyroid conditions (bamboo shoot goitrogens, large regular amounts)
items.preparation: Use as a souring condiment in stews; fermentation and cooking together neutralize the raw shoot's harshness.

items.name: Kinema (fermented soybean)
items.prabhava: Sticky-strand fermented soybean of the Nepal-Sikkim belt — the Himalayan natto; fermentation unlocks the bean's protein for weak mountain-winter digestion.
items.preparation: Fry briefly then simmer into curry; the ammonia-edge mellows with cooking, the digestibility is fermentation's gift.

items.name: Hawaijar (fermented soybean)
items.prabhava: Manipur's alkaline soybean ferment, sibling to kinema and natto — umami backbone of eromba and a winter protein of the valley.
items.preparation: Mash into chili-vegetable stews; like kinema, its power is predigested protein with a strong voice.

items.name: Neera (fresh palm sap)
items.prabhava: Dawn-tapped palm sap before fermentation — mineral-rich, cooling and mildly laxative; hours later it becomes toddy, which is another substance entirely.
combinations: drunk fresh at dawn, chilled in clay
boiled down into palm jaggery when surplus
contraindications: ferments within hours — sour or fizzy neera is becoming alcoholic toddy
items.preparation: Drink within hours of tapping, kept cool; classical texts distinguish fresh tala rasa (wholesome) from fermented (intoxicating).
provenance: Tamil-Kerala-Bengal palm tradition; tala in nighantus

items.name: Khalpi (fermented cucumber)
items.prabhava: Nepal's ripe-cucumber ferment — sun-cured chunks soured in their own brine; a rare cucumber preparation that warms instead of cools.
combinations: dressed with mustard oil and chili
items.preparation: Ripe yellow cucumbers, sun-wilted and fermented in brine 3–5 days; serve as a probiotic pickle course.
